title: Induced matchings in the regular 4-polytopes
statement: An induced (strong) matching is a set of edges, no two sharing a vertex and no two joined by an edge of the graph. Determine the largest size of an induced matching for the graphs of the six regular convex 4-polytopes (the 5-cell K5; the tesseract, 16 vertices; the 16-cell, 8 vertices; the 24-cell, 24 vertices, 8-regular; the 600-cell, 120 vertices, 12-regular; the 120-cell, 600 vertices, 4-regular) and of the two E8 polytopes 3_21 (Gosset, 56 vertices, 27-regular) and 4_21 (the 240 roots of E8, 56-regular), each vertex adjacent to its nearest neighbours. First values (ours): the 5-cell 1 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 4 (exact); the 16-cell 1 (exact); the 24-cell 4 (exact); the 600-cell 13; the 120-cell 139; the Gosset polytope 3_21 3 (exact); the E8 root polytope 4_21 7. The headline cell is the 120-cell: find a certificate with value 140 or more (the packing bound |M| (2d - 1) <= nd/2: <= 171 for the 120-cell), or prove 139 optimal.
submission: Text file: one edge 'u v' per line (vertex numbers in the checker's vertex order) (the 120-cell).
score: the number of edges (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 139 for the 120-cell, best found: CP-SAT (one worker, 5 to 60 seconds) on the model of tools/polytope_sets.py, or, for zero forcing and power domination, greedy completion and pruning between rounds of fort cuts

context: Induced matchings (Stockmeyer and Vazirani 1982, Cameron 1989) bound the strong chromatic index, model interference-free transmissions in radio networks, and are NP-hard to maximise. Their values are known for hypercubes and grids; for the other regular 4-polytopes and the E8 polytopes nothing was found. In a d-regular graph the 2d - 1 edges touching one edge of an induced matching touch no other edge of it (an edge between two of them is forbidden), so |M| (2d - 1) <= nd/2: at most 31 for the 600-cell, 171 for the 120-cell, 14 for 3_21 and 60 for 4_21. How close the matchings come to this packing bound is open.
references: L. J. Stockmeyer, V. V. Vazirani, NP-completeness of some generalizations of the maximum matching problem, Inform. Process. Lett. 15 (1982) 14-19
K. Cameron, Induced matchings, Discrete Appl. Math. 24 (1989) 97-102
H. S. M. Coxeter, Regular Polytopes (3rd ed., Dover 1973)

novelty.verdict: new. No induced matching result for the 600-cell, the 120-cell, the 24-cell or the E8 polytopes (searched with E8 and Gosset) was found on arXiv, in the journal literature (Crossref) or by web search; the known values for hypercubes and complete graphs cover only the small cells.
closest: General results on induced matching (the references) and its values for hypercubes, grids and products; none for these polytopes.
Our polytope problems (polytope-ising, potts3-600, cell600-idcode, cell600-forest, cell120-coil, e8-idcode, e8-resolving): other invariants of the same graphs.
